sampling_model.design: Complete randomization draws \(W\) uniformly from assignments with exactly \(m\) treated units; the design variable includes the integer \(m\) and the common local channel \(Q\).
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) labeled units and both binary potential outcomes are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The private input \((W_i,Y_i(W_i))\) belongs to \(\mathcal X\), and the analyst does not separately observe \(W_i\) or \(Y_i(W_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The treatment count obeys \(1\le m<N\); no propensity model is estimated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The nuisance is the full finite schedule orbit \(n\in\mathcal O_N\); inference imposes coverage for every orbit and does not estimate a superpopulation regression.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: A finite family of extremal mechanisms, which we call staircase mechanisms, contains the optimal privatization mechanism.
Using a customized privacy mechanism, we can match the lower bound, giving minimax optimal inference.
Both of the resulting \(1-\alpha\) confidence sets are exact.
Inverting the likelihood ratio test minimizes the probability of including false values in the confidence region.
The same non-asymptotic confidence intervals hold for the sample average treatment effect.
We provide a sequence of values, returned by semidefinite programs, finitely converges to the minimal value.
Every extreme point of the fixed-output joint range is attained by a sort--partition--randomize mechanism.

body.tldr: Exact finite-population causal inference under local privacy is formulated as a joint choice of treatment count, common channel, and randomized confidence rule. Schedule permutation and a constructive Blackwell refinement reduce the problem to a fourteen-pattern, degree-\(N\) polynomial game with an inner exact confidence linear program. The four-unit game already has a certified nonbinary regime and a global value bracket. The paper's kernel is an optimizer-attaining algebraic certificate that persists on a nonempty parameter cell and locates an actual endpoint of the region where balanced binary-partition randomized response is globally optimal.

project_justification.gap: Existing causal local-privacy theory optimizes population estimation risk or asymptotic confidence width, exact randomization inference fixes a nonprivate observation experiment, and staircase optimality applies to convex single-draw utilities. Their intersection leaves the exact common-channel SATE confidence game and its design boundaries unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary schedule, complete-randomization orbit structure, and four protected input values make the causal nuisance finite while preserving the nonconvex product-channel difficulty.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a lossless orbit and channel reduction, exact primal--dual confidence inference, an attained polynomial formulation, certified nonbinary evidence, and an algebraic continuation method culminating in one sign-certified balanced-binary phase boundary.

body.related_work: Ohnishi and Awan (2025) provide the causal-local-privacy motivation and distinguish joint from customized privatization, but their targets are population MSE and plug-in inference. Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) provide exact finite-population SATE inversion with binary outcomes when the assignment and observed outcomes are available. Schafer and Stark (2009) provide the least-favorable-prior view of minimax expected-size confidence regions for a fixed experiment. Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath (2016) provide the staircase geometry for convex column-separable privacy utilities; their proof does not cover the optimized common-channel confidence value. Chen, Cormode, Bharadwaj, Romov, and Ozgur (2024) treat privacy mechanism and allocation as an experiment-design problem under distributed privacy, but do not derive exact schedulewise phase boundaries. Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa (2026) identify sort--partition--randomize mechanisms for simple binary testing, while the present nuisance contains many schedule nulls and no common likelihood-ratio ordering. Mai (2023) informs the exact positivity machinery, and Bienstock, Del Pia, and Hildebrand (2023) caution that algebraic rather than rational certificates may be necessary.
body.technical_internal_limitation: At \((N,\alpha,\lambda)=(4,2/5,1000)\), the independently reproduced unrestricted bounds differ by \(5.94\times10^{-6}\). This certifies the value to positive tolerance and excludes all unbalanced allocations and balanced binary partitions nearby, but it does not identify a globally minimizing channel. The continuation handle must close this mathematical gap rather than report additional decimal precision.
body.honest_scope: The orbit kernel, fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, fixed-channel primal--dual program, degree-\(N\) attainment, nonconvexity diagnostic, and the displayed four-unit certificates have concrete derivations or exact finite checks that must be rewritten as proofs. The optimizer-attaining cell and actual boundary are open. The project does not claim four-output sufficiency, general-\(N\) balance, practical gains at \(95\%\) coverage, or equivalence to a protocol that reveals assignment. At \(\lambda=1\) the value reduces to \((2N+1)(1-\alpha)\); without privacy and with revealed assignment the setup reduces to classical exact SATE randomization inversion.
